title: 1 Timothy Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Timothy chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Timothy Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Timothy Chapter 1.

questions.question: In 1 Timothy 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ
Charity out of a pure heart
questions.correctAnswer: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: The first mention in the chapter is about Paul being an apostle of Jesus Christ, as stated in 1 Timothy 1:1.

questions.question: Who is addressed as 'my own son in the faith'?
questions.explanation: Timothy is referred to as 'my own son in the faith' in 1 Timothy 1:2.

questions.question: What does Paul wish for Timothy in 1 Timothy 1:2?
questions.explanation: Paul wishes 'Grace, mercy, and peace' for Timothy as stated in 1 Timothy 1:2.

questions.question: Where did Paul ask Timothy to abide?
questions.explanation: Paul besought Timothy to abide still at Ephesus according to 1 Timothy 1:3.

questions.question: What was Timothy asked to charge some to do?
questions.explanation: Timothy was to charge some that they teach no other doctrine as mentioned in 1 Timothy 1:3.

questions.question: What should people not give heed to according to 1 Timothy 1:4?
questions.explanation: The verse states that one should not give heed to fables and endless genealogies as stated in 1 Timothy 1:4.

questions.question: What is the end of the commandment according to 1 Timothy 1:5?
options: Charity out of a pure heart
questions.correctAnswer: Charity out of a pure heart
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:5 states that the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart.

questions.question: What have some turned aside to according to 1 Timothy 1:6?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that some have turned aside unto vain jangling as mentioned in 1 Timothy 1:6.

questions.question: What were some desiring to be according to 1 Timothy 1:7?
questions.explanation: The verse states that some were desiring to be teachers of the law as per 1 Timothy 1:7.

questions.question: Do these teachers understand what they say according to 1 Timothy 1:7?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:7 states that they understand neither what they say, nor whereof they affirm.

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 1:5, what should the commandment end in?
questions.explanation: The commandment ends in charity out of a pure heart, a good conscience, and faith unfeigned, as implied in 1 Timothy 1:5.

questions.question: True or False: Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
questions.explanation: The verse confirms that Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ in 1 Timothy 1:1.

questions.question: True or False: Timothy was told to avoid teaching charity.
questions.explanation: The instructions given do not include teaching charity but rather caution against teaching other doctrines, as per 1 Timothy 1:3.

questions.question: True or False: The end of the commandment is to create confusion.
questions.explanation: The end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, not confusion, as stated in 1 Timothy 1:5.

questions.question: True or False: Some have turned aside unto godly edifying.
questions.explanation: The text states that some have turned aside unto vain jangling, not godly edifying, in 1 Timothy 1:6.

medium.title: 1 Timothy Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Timothy Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 1:8, what do we know about the law?
options: The law is good, if a man use it lawfully
The law is outdated and unnecessary
The law is only for the Jews
The law brings condemnation to all
questions.correctAnswer: The law is good, if a man use it lawfully
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:8 states, 'But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully.'

questions.question: What does 1 Timothy 1:10 indicate is contrary to sound doctrine?
options: Charity out of a pure heart
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:10 lists 'For whoremongers... and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine.'

questions.question: Who does Paul thank for enabling him for ministry according to 1 Timothy 1:12?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:12 states, 'And I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who hath enabled me...'

questions.question: What is the purpose of the commandment mentioned in 1 Timothy 1:5?
options: To promote charity out of a pure heart
questions.correctAnswer: To promote charity out of a pure heart
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:5 says, 'Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart...'

questions.question: What was Paul’s state before obtaining mercy according to 1 Timothy 1:13?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:13 states, 'Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor...'

questions.question: What does 1 Timothy 1:14 say the grace of the Lord was?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:14 details that 'the grace of our Lord was exceeding abundant...'

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 1:9, the law is not made for which type of man?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:9 states, 'the law is not made for a righteous man...'

questions.question: What does 1 Timothy 1:6 say some have turned aside unto?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:6 mentions, 'From which some having swerved have turned aside unto vain jangling.'

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 1:11, what was committed to Paul's trust?
options: The glorious gospel of the blessed God
questions.correctAnswer: The glorious gospel of the blessed God
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 1 Timothy 1:11 states, 'According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.'

questions.question: What does 1 Timothy 1:7 say about certain teachers of the law?
options: They desire to teach without understanding
They are leading many to righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: They desire to teach without understanding
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:7 indicates, 'Desiring to be teachers of the law; understanding neither what they say, nor whereof they affirm.'

questions.question: What is the necessary attitude of a Christian according to 1 Timothy 1:5?
options: Charity out of a pure heart
questions.correctAnswer: Charity out of a pure heart
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:5 states, 'Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart...'

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 1:14, what accompanies the abundant grace of the Lord?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:14 mentions, 'the grace of our Lord was exceeding abundant with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.'

questions.question: Is it true that Paul considered himself a blasphemer before receiving mercy?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:13 states, 'Who was before a blasphemer... but I obtained mercy...'

questions.question: Is it false that the law is for the righteous according to 1 Timothy 1:9?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:9 clearly states that the law is not made for a righteous man.

questions.question: Is it false that sound doctrine is contrary to blasphemy according to 1 Timothy 1:10?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Timothy 1:10 indicates that blasphemy is indeed contrary to sound doctrine.

hard.title: 1 Timothy Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Timothy Chapter 1.

questions.question: What does Paul declare about Christ Jesus in 1 Timothy 1:15?
options: He came to condemn the righteous.
He came to establish a new law.
He came to teach the wise.
questions.explanation: This is stated directly in 1 Timothy 1:15: 'that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.'

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 1:16, why did Paul obtain mercy?
options: To lead many to the law.
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:16 states that Paul obtained mercy, 'that in me first Jesus Christ might shew forth all longsuffering.'

questions.question: What title is given to God in 1 Timothy 1:17?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:17 refers to God as 'the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God.'

questions.question: What charge does Paul give Timothy in 1 Timothy 1:18?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:18 contains the charge: 'that thou by them mightest war a good warfare.'

questions.question: What happens to those who put away faith and a good conscience according to 1 Timothy 1:19?
options: They make shipwreck of their faith.
questions.correctAnswer: They make shipwreck of their faith.
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:19 warns that 'some having put away concerning faith have made shipwreck.'

questions.question: Who does Paul mention specifically as having been delivered unto Satan in 1 Timothy 1:20?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:20 names Hymenaeus and Alexander as those Paul has delivered unto Satan.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'mercy' in 1 Timothy 1:16 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word for 'mercy' refers to compassion or kindness shown to someone in need.

questions.question: What literary device is used in 1 Timothy 1:17 when Paul refers to God?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'King eternal' and the concluding 'forever and ever' create an inclusio around the description of God.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of mercy found in 1 Timothy 1:16?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:4-5 speaks of God's great love and mercy in saving us, echoing the theme from 1 Timothy 1:16.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of battling against blasphemy as mentioned in 1 Timothy 1:20?
questions.explanation: Titus 1:10-11 discusses silencing those who blaspheme, connecting with the warning in 1 Timothy 1:20.

questions.question: What comes before the declaration in 1 Timothy 1:15?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:14 precedes it, where Paul expresses gratitude for the abundant grace he received.

questions.question: What comes after the charge given to Timothy in 1 Timothy 1:18?
options: A reminder of faith and a good conscience.
questions.correctAnswer: A reminder of faith and a good conscience.
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:19 follows, reminding Timothy of the importance of holding faith and a good conscience.

questions.question: The statement that Paul was a blasphemer, found in 1 Timothy 1:13, is an example of what type of literary device?
questions.explanation: Paul contrasts his past as a blasphemer with his current state of being saved, demonstrating an antithesis of transformation.

questions.question: The statement 'Holding faith, and a good conscience' in 1 Timothy 1:19 means what?
questions.explanation: This is a true statement as 1 Timothy 1:19 emphasizes the importance of maintaining faith and a good conscience.

questions.question: 1 Timothy 1:20 indicates that Hymenaeus and Alexander were examples of faithful servants.
questions.explanation: This is false because 1 Timothy 1:20 describes them as being delivered unto Satan for their blasphemy.

theological.title: 1 Timothy Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Timothy Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Timothy 1:5 teach about the nature of sanctification?
options: Sanctification is grounded in charity from a pure heart, a good conscience, and unfeigned faith
Sanctification is primarily about rigorous adherence to the law
Sanctification depends on genealogical heritage and ritual observance
Sanctification is achieved through endless doctrinal debates
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification is grounded in charity from a pure heart, a good conscience, and unfeigned faith
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:5 states that the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, a good conscience, and faith unfeigned, indicating that sanctification is a moral and spiritual transformation grounded in love and genuine faith rather than legalism or external forms.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Timothy 1:8 teach about the proper use of the law?
options: The law is good if used lawfully
The law is obsolete for Christians
The law is only for the Jewish people
The law is primarily ceremonial and non-binding
questions.correctAnswer: The law is good if used lawfully
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:8 clearly states that the law is good if a man uses it lawfully, affirming that the law remains a valid moral guide when rightly understood and applied.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin does 1 Timothy 1:9 teach?
options: The law is made not for the righteous but for the lawless and disobedient
All humans are righteous by nature and do not need the law
Sin is primarily a ceremonial impurity, not moral rebellion
The law condemns only external acts, not internal attitudes
questions.correctAnswer: The law is made not for the righteous but for the lawless and disobedient
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:9 specifies that the law is not made for the righteous but for sinners and the lawless, emphasizing that the law’s purpose is to restrain and condemn those who live in disobedience to God’s moral standards.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Timothy 1:16 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:16 shows that Jesus Christ demonstrated longsuffering in showing mercy to Paul, serving as a pattern for believers, highlighting God's patience with sinners.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Timothy 1:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:17 calls God the King eternal, immortal, invisible, emphasizing His eternal and unchanging nature, which is fundamental to biblical theology.

questions.question: How does 1 Timothy 1:3-4 prepare for the biblical theme of sound doctrine and church order found elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It warns against false teachings and genealogies, preparing the church to maintain doctrinal purity
It encourages freedom to teach any doctrine according to personal preference
It minimizes the importance of doctrine in favor of ritual
It promotes endless debates as the means to faith
questions.correctAnswer: It warns against false teachings and genealogies, preparing the church to maintain doctrinal purity
questions.explanation: Verses 3-4 urge Timothy to command certain people not to teach other doctrines or give heed to fables and endless genealogies, establishing the necessity of sound teaching consistent with biblical doctrine (cf. Titus 1:9).

questions.question: How does 1 Timothy 1:12-13 connect the redemptive-historical theme of grace with the apostle Paul's personal testimony?
options: It shows that God’s grace is able to redeem even the worst sinners, fulfilling God’s redemptive plan
It suggests Paul was an exception to God’s usual grace
It emphasizes human effort over divine grace
It denies that Paul ever needed mercy
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that God’s grace is able to redeem even the worst sinners, fulfilling God’s redemptive plan
questions.explanation: Paul’s testimony in verses 12-13 illustrates the doctrine of grace by showing how God mercifully saved him despite his past as a blasphemer and persecutor, exemplifying the power of divine mercy in salvation history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 Timothy 1:14 and 1 Timothy 1:15 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is by the abundant grace of Christ Jesus who came to save sinners
Salvation depends on human works and strict law-keeping
Salvation is limited to the righteous only
Salvation is primarily about ethnic heritage
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is by the abundant grace of Christ Jesus who came to save sinners
questions.explanation: Verse 14 emphasizes the exceeding abundant grace with faith and love in Christ Jesus, while verse 15 affirms that Jesus came to save sinners, together teaching salvation by grace through faith, centered on Christ’s mission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 Timothy 1:18 and 1 Timothy 1:19 teach about Christian perseverance?
options: Believers must hold onto faith and a good conscience to avoid shipwrecking their faith
Perseverance is irrelevant as salvation is guaranteed without effort
Faith alone, without conscience, suffices for perseverance
Conscience alone, without faith, ensures perseverance
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must hold onto faith and a good conscience to avoid shipwrecking their faith
questions.explanation: These verses exhort Timothy to wage a good warfare holding faith and a good conscience, warning that some have rejected these and made shipwreck of their faith, teaching the necessity of both faith and moral integrity in perseverance.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Timothy 1:6 and 1 Timothy 1:7 teach about false teachers?
options: False teachers engage in vain jangling and desire to be teachers without understanding
False teachers have a deep and proper understanding of the law
False teachers avoid disputes and focus on edification
False teachers are primarily motivated by love and faith
questions.correctAnswer: False teachers engage in vain jangling and desire to be teachers without understanding
questions.explanation: Verse 6 notes some have swerved to vain jangling, and verse 7 adds that they desire to be teachers of the law without understanding, identifying the nature and motivation of false teachers.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 1 Timothy 1:9-10 contradicts modern ethics by listing sins that seem outdated or culturally specific. What does 1 Timothy 1:9-10 actually teach?
options: The law targets all forms of lawlessness and moral rebellion contrary to sound doctrine
The law only condemns ceremonial impurities irrelevant today
The law is obsolete and irrelevant for Christians
The law endorses some sinful behaviors as culturally acceptable
questions.correctAnswer: The law targets all forms of lawlessness and moral rebellion contrary to sound doctrine
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:9-10 lists various sins including murderers, liars, and blasphemers, emphasizing that the law is designed against all ungodliness and sinners, affirming timeless moral standards rather than cultural specifics.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Timothy 1:20 teach about church discipline?
options: False teachers like Hymenaeus and Alexander can be delivered to Satan for correction
Church discipline is unnecessary and tolerance is paramount
Blasphemy is tolerated within the church for freedom of speech
Discipline should be limited to private rebuke only
questions.correctAnswer: False teachers like Hymenaeus and Alexander can be delivered to Satan for correction
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:20 shows that severe church discipline including delivering to Satan is used for those who blaspheme, indicating the seriousness of protecting sound doctrine in the church.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 1 Timothy 1:12 in relation to Paul's ministry?
options: Sovereignty in enabling and appointing Paul to the ministry
Immutability in never changing God's plan
Omnipotence in performing miracles through Paul
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty in enabling and appointing Paul to the ministry
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 1:12 shows Christ Jesus enabling Paul and counting him faithful, illustrating God's sovereign choice and empowerment in calling ministers for His purposes.

questions.question: What theological significance does 1 Timothy 1:11 have regarding the gospel message?
options: The gospel is described as glorious and committed to Paul’s trust
The gospel is a human invention subject to revision
The gospel is secondary to the law
The gospel is a private secret for a select few
questions.correctAnswer: The gospel is described as glorious and committed to Paul’s trust
questions.explanation: Verse 11 emphasizes the glorious gospel of the blessed God which was entrusted to Paul, affirming both the divine origin and authoritative stewardship of the gospel message.

questions.question: How does 1 Timothy 1:2 contribute to understanding the relational nature of salvation?
options: Salvation is relational, involving grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Jesus Christ
Salvation is purely transactional without personal relationship
Salvation excludes mercy in favor of justice only
Salvation is impersonal and only involves God the Father
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is relational, involving grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: The greeting in 1 Timothy 1:2 invokes grace, mercy, and peace from both God the Father and Jesus Christ, highlighting the Trinitarian and relational dimensions of salvation.
